chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

“ʿAlī عليه السلام would not perform any prayer during the night, once he had performed the ʿatamah prayer, until the middle of the night; and he would not perform any prayer during the day until the sun had passed the meridian.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: What I act upon is what is contained in this hadith and the one before it: that it is not permissible to perform any of the supererogatory prayers of zawāl before zawāl. And a concession has also been narrated regarding the permissibility of performing them earlier.

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: the sun’s decline from the meridian, marking noon time
key_terms.الْعَتَمَةَ: the night prayer, referring here to the ʿIshāʾ prayer
key_terms.تَزُولَ: declines or passes the meridian; used for the sun at noon
key_terms.رُخْصَةٌ: a concession or dispensation permitting an easier ruling
key_terms.نَوَافِلِ: supererogatory prayers performed in addition to the obligatory prayers
key_terms.يَنْتَصِفَ: reaches the midpoint; here, when the night reaches its middle

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform the nawāfil of zawāl before noon in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the timing of supererogatory prayers, indicating that Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام would not pray at night after the ʿIshāʾ prayer until midnight, nor during the day until the sun passed the meridian. Shaykh al-Ṭūsī states that he acts upon the ruling that the nawāfil of zawāl should not be performed before zawāl, while acknowledging that a reported concession exists allowing earlier performance.
